title: Prepare a safety-team brief
description: Bring research, FDA statements and the label together.
question: Prepare a brief for our drug-safety team on tofacitinib cardiovascular risk. Compare ORAL Surveillance and STAR-RA, explain what the FDA safety communication and indexed prescribing information say, and identify uncertainties for human review.

title: Why do the studies differ?
description: Compare study design, patient groups and uncertainty.
question: Compare the design and patient populations of ORAL Surveillance and STAR-RA. How could those differences affect interpretation of cardiovascular findings, and what can the indexed abstracts not establish?

title: Did FDA remove the warning?
description: Separate a research finding from a regulatory action.
question: Does the STAR-RA result by itself establish that FDA withdrew its tofacitinib warning? Compare the actual research, FDA communication and indexed label.

title: What does the label say?
description: Inspect cardiovascular warnings in a dated label version.
question: What cardiovascular warnings and study results are stated in the indexed Xeljanz prescribing information? Identify the version date and distinguish the label's statements from the research findings.

title: What was available in 2021?
description: Exclude newer papers and the later label snapshot.
question: Prepare a tofacitinib safety brief from the indexed FDA, research and label sources available by the cutoff.

title: What if no sources qualify?
description: Use a 2020 cutoff and see the agent acknowledge the gap.
question: Prepare a tofacitinib safety brief from the indexed FDA, research and label sources available by the cutoff.
